market_holds: The HDL ADS (1 ADS = 10 HK shares, by my parity arithmetic) hardly trades: 20-day average 75 ADS a day per the sealed baseline, zero-volume days are common, and the last print was 9.81 on 2026-11-23 (800 ADS). Price discovery happens in Hong Kong (9658.HK), which closed at HKD 7.96 on 2026-11-24 (+1.4%). At USDHKD 7.841 that is about USD 10.15 an ADS. Over 139 2026 days with ADS volume, the ADS has traded at a mean -0.9% to HK parity, sd 2.0 points. The 9.81 print is 3.4% under today's parity. Neither line has an option market or consensus: Earnings Whispers' Q2 estimates are visibly broken, and three brokers rate it Buy with stale targets. HK is down 29% since the Q2 print (11.11 to 7.85), against -21% for Haidilao 6862.HK and -13% for the HSI over the same dates, so most of the slide is the market and the brand, and the stock sits near its 52-week low (sealed run-up 20d -6.5%, 0.7% off the low). The release comes before the US open, after the HK close of 25 Nov (Q2: HK reacted the next day at -6.9%). So the HK session inside the window trades before the result. On past report days the ADS traded little and often at stale prices. Q2 (2026-08-26): the ADS printed 13.95, unchanged, through the morning, so 0% at 13:00 ET, while HK fell 6.9% the next day. Q1 (2026-05-20): +3.0% by 11:30 ET, and HK +2.3% the next day. Report-day close-to-close moves were -2.1% (Q3 2025, 2025-11-26 per the Q3 2025 release date), -2.8% (Q4 2025, 2026-03-31) and +3.0% and +1.3% (2026).
view: Inside this window the print hardly decides the move. The ADS's microstructure does. The entry price is a stale 9.81 trade unless someone prints before today's close, and no 5-minute bar today shows volume as of 14:25 ET. The next trades on 25 Nov will be set against HK parity, about 10.06-10.15 on today's HK close, plus whatever the release says. On fundamentals the headline should be benign to good. Q3 2025 net profit was only USD 3.6m after a USD 31.7m larger FX loss. In Q3 2026 the currencies that caused this year's FX losses mostly strengthened against the dollar (end-Jun to end-Sep 2026, FRED: KRW 1548.8 to 1355.9, JPY 162.6 to 157.3, SGD 1.294 to 1.277; MYR flat; THB 33.24 to 33.60, weaker). That points to an FX gain or a much smaller loss, so 'net profit up several-fold' is a likely headline. Operating income also has an easy comparison (Q3 2025 USD 12.6m, -15.4%), after +70.7% in Q1 and +119% in Q2. Singapore F&B was flat to slightly positive (restaurants +2.6% YoY in September). The risks are same-store sales (Q2 total -0.8%, North America -8.5%) and the HK market's habit of selling good-looking prints. All of that resolves mostly in HK on 26 Nov, after the window. Net: a mild upward lean from the parity gap and a probably flattering headline, cut down by a real chance the ADS does not trade by 13:00 (a 0% move, inside the 2.85% deadband) or trades at a stale price, as it did in Q2.
unpriced: Two small things, neither strong enough to trade. (1) The last ADS print, 9.81, sits about 3% below parity with today's HK close, about 2.4% after the usual -0.9% discount; a thin quote that is behind its underlying. (2) Q3 2026 FX, read off FRED: KRW +12.5%, JPY +3.4% and SGD +1.3% against the dollar should flip this year's FX-loss line, so the YoY net profit headline is likely to look strong. Nobody publishes a usable consensus that shows this is modelled. Whether the thin US market acts on it before 13:00 ET is doubtful.

recommendation.reason: The best-evidenced edge is the stale ADS quote against HK parity plus an FX-flattered net profit headline. But the ADS trades a few hundred shares a day and has often not repriced inside the morning window: in Q2 it printed unchanged at 13:00 ET before HK fell 6.9% the next day. With a real chance of no trade, or a stale one, before 13:00, and HK's pre-result session on 25 Nov unknown, the probability is well short of 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A weak same-store sales line (total SSS down several percent, or North America or Southeast Asia turnover falling) or a cautious call at 07:00 ET, priced by an early ADS trade below 9.8. Or a sharp HK fall in the 25 Nov session, which would erase the parity gap before the release.

self_critique: The parity gap is not an edge if nobody trades the ADS before 13:00. The Q2 report day showed the morning print sitting at the stale prior close. HK's pre-result session on 25 Nov could also fall and close the gap. The FX-flattered headline could be outweighed by weak same-store sales, which fell in Q2 with North America down 8.5%, and HK sold the last print 6.9%. And if someone prints the ADS near parity before today's close, the entry moves up and the gap disappears.
approach_notes: P6 (find where the reaction is actually decided) was the useful part. Here that was the ADS's microstructure against HK parity and the release timing, not the line the print is read on. P3's breadth of sources mattered less for a 13:00 ET window on a near-untraded ADS whose real reaction happens in HK the next day. The playbook has no guidance for a dual-listed name whose scored line barely trades.
